note: Precomputed solver output for offline demos: every frame comes from the pandapower AC power flow and the EPANET 2.2 extended-period hydraulic simulation (via WNTR) of the synthetic district, generated by `npm run sim:export`. Replays are recorded simulation results, not live telemetry.

definition.name: Electrical Feeder Failure
definition.description: A permanent fault on Feeder F3 trips the lateral recloser at 17:00, de-energising the west district: City Hospital (B32) and Pumping Station PS-2 (B33) lose grid supply. The hospital's genset carries its life-safety load, but the genset does not supply water; the West pressure zone now depends on Tank T2.
narrative: 17:00 — fault on Feeder F3 (line B27–B28); recloser SW-06-26 trips and the whole lateral B26–B33 goes dark.
City Hospital transfers to its 150 kW genset; PS-2 stops and the West zone rides on Tank T2 storage.
17:02 — the faulted section is isolated and the healthy upstream section is re-energised.
17:05 — recovery candidates are generated, evaluated with the coupled power–water simulation and verified.
17:10 — the selected switching plan is executed; the extended-period hydraulic simulation shows what happens to Tank T2 and hospital pressure over the evening.

definition.name: Critical Pump Power Loss
definition.description: On a warm evening (electrical demand 5% above the base scenario) a fault on the cable that feeds Pumping Station PS-2 (line B32–B33) removes supply from PS-2's bus. After isolation the electrical outage is small, but PS-2 is the only pump of the West pressure zone: the hospital's water service now depends on Tank T2 — or on back-feeding PS-2 through tie SW-18-33 from the weak end of Feeder F1.
narrative: 17:00 — fault on the PS-2 supply cable (line B32–B33); recloser SW-06-26 trips the Feeder F3 lateral.
17:02 — SW-32-33 isolates the faulted cable and the lateral is reclosed: every bus except B33 is back, including the hospital.
The remaining electrical outage is about 80 kW — but it is the West zone's only pump.
PS-2 can only be re-energised through tie SW-18-33 from B18, the weakest point of the feeder; at the evening peak that route sits right at the 0.90 pu voltage limit.

Restoring PS-2 therefore needs voltage headroom: interrupting a few supplied customers on the F1 tail. Conventional restoration never interrupts supplied customers for one pump; the coupled planner weighs that against the hospital's water service.

definition.name: High-Demand Conditions
definition.description: A hot evening pushes electrical demand to 125% and water demand to 115% of the base scenario, then the same Feeder F3 fault strikes. Voltage and thermal margins are tight, so fewer restoration options satisfy every hard limit and the West zone drains faster without PS-2.
narrative: Evening heat: electrical demand ×1.25 and water demand ×1.15 relative to the base scenario.
17:00 — the same fault on Feeder F3 (line B27–B28) trips recloser SW-06-26.
Tank T2 drains faster than in the base case while PS-2 is without supply.
Tighter voltage and thermal margins reject more restoration candidates; full restoration is not achievable within the hard limits.
The comparison shows which loads each strategy restores and what that means for hospital water pressure.
